merged.title: fix(port): the library layer answers as the console's libraries and kernel do
merged.author: Drustburn
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

The port answers the game's calls into Sony's libraries and the EE
kernel with host C of its own (`port/game/common/lib/*`, bound by each
game's `libraries.tsv`). A differential test against calls recorded
from the retail game in an emulator found places where those answers
differ from what the console's libraries and kernel give: return values
the kernel never returns, state kept in the port's statics where the
library keeps it in the game's memory, a guard that consulted a table
the console does not have, packets in the wrong layout, and library
functions answered by the port that only keep the game's own state and
can run the game's C. This PR fixes them.

Most of them change nothing a player sees in rac1 today (no caller
reads the value, or both sides happen to agree in a normal run); they
make the library layer's answers and the game's memory match the
console's, which is what the game's own code relies on. Where a commit
has a game-visible effect it says so.

merged.title: feat(port): the EE's float arithmetic for chosen functions, and port overrides of matched C
merged.author: Drustburn
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Two pieces of infrastructure the port's remaining fixes build on, each
with one small real use as proof.

**1. The EE FPU's float arithmetic for C (`openrac/ps2float.h`,
hostgen.json `"ps2_float"`).** The port computes the game's floats in the
host's arithmetic, with the game's thread rounding toward zero and
denormals as zero (`openrac_ee_float_mode`) and `openrac_fdiv`'s
saturating divide. That is the EE's arithmetic for most of what the game
computes, but not all of it: the EE's adder drops the smaller operand's
bits more than one place below the larger one's last bit before it adds
(`1 - 1.5 * 2^-24` is `0x3F7FFFFF` on the console, `0x3F7FFFFE` on a host
rounding toward zero), a result past the largest float is `±0x7FFFFFFF`
(an infinity or FLT_MAX on the host), and an exponent of 255 is an
ordinary number. Where the game cuts a result to an integer, or compares
it, one last place decides. `port/assets/ps2_float.h` already models the
console's arithmetic on bit patterns

merged.title: Add enhanced lighting and GPU-driven rendering
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Adds optional enhanced rendering with baked probe GI, GTAO, sun shadows and Ratchet shadows. Normal builds keep the original lighting.

The core Vulkan rendering optimisations also benefit normal rendering, without enabling enhanced lighting:

- Batch compatible opaque draws using shared geometry and material buffers.
- Reduce draw calls, resource bindings and CPU submission overhead.
- Specialise shaders, reuse the depth prepass and improve visibility culling.

Enhanced rendering also adds batched shadow draws and a shadow atlas, parallel probe baking, per-level settings, sparse and dense probe regions, and an all-level bake script. Optional GPU profiling labels and documentation cover the rendering and baking workflows.

A separate fix avoids double frame pacing when asynchronous vsync is active.

Enhanced lighting is very much a work in progress. Interiors do not yet have correct lighting, and each level still needs bespoke attention. Probe baking is slow and has yet to be optimised
